title: Spectrally local geometric response at the onset of many-body quantum chaos
abstract: We introduce the spectral density of geometric response, a measure of eigenstate sensitivity across an energy spectrum. Applied to many-body quantum systems, it reveals an exponentially sensitive integrability-to-chaos crossover, where eigenbasis deformations first accumulate in localized spectral regions before spreading throughout the spectrum. Physically motivated random-matrix ensembles reproduce this behaviour, whereas Gaussian ensembles do not, indicating universal features of the route to chaos that are absent from featureless random-matrix models.
summary: This paper introduces the spectral density of geometric response as a diagnostic tool to study how many-body quantum systems transition from integrable to chaotic behavior. It reveals that this crossover involves an initial localization of eigenbasis deformations before they spread across the spectrum. The findings suggest universal features governing chaos onset that are not captured by simple random matrix models.
main_problem: The paper investigates how quantum systems transition from integrable regimes towards chaos, focusing on spectral properties.
main_result: It finds that the crossover to chaos is characterized by an exponentially sensitive accumulation of eigenbasis deformations in localized spectral regions before spreading out.
method: The authors introduce and analyze a novel diagnostic tool called the 'spectral density of geometric response' to measure eigenstate sensitivity across the energy spectrum.
model_or_system: The study is applied to general many-body quantum systems, comparing results from physically motivated random-matrix ensembles against featureless Gaussian ensembles.
key_observables: Spectral density of geometric response; accumulation and spreading of eigenbasis deformations.
important_parameters: Integrability-to-chaos crossover scale; energy spectrum structure.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing physical random matrix models against idealized Gaussian ensembles to isolate universal features.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the spectral density of geometric response, applies it to many-body systems to characterize the integrability-to-chaos crossover, and contrasts the findings between different random matrix models.
why_interesting: This work provides a quantitative measure (spectral density) for tracking the onset of quantum chaos in complex many-body dynamics, which is relevant for understanding thermalization and energy transport in interacting systems.
